---
title: "Rene Coig's R Notebook for Clustering Analysis"
date: 11/30/22
---

This notebook tests the hypothesis that age by sex trajectories in US mortality data can be used to identify physiological vs external influences on disease incidence.
Sex-specific cancers that are solely driven by biology should cluster more frequently with more biologically driven diseases, whereas external causes should cluster more frequently with environmentally driven sex differences in diseases.

Load package and data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(reshape2)
#data_GACod <- read.csv("1999-2019_Gender-Age-byCauseofDeathALL.csv",header=T)
data_GACod <- read.csv("1999-2019_Gender_byAge45andup_10-year-groups_byCauseofDeath.csv",header=T)
Lifetime <- read.csv("1999-2019_Gender_AllAges_byCauseofDeath.csv",header=T)
codes<-read.csv("Hierarchy.csv",header=T)
desc<-read.csv("categories.csv",header=T)
#install.packages("cluster")
#install.packages("dendextend")
#install.packages("corrplot")
#install.packages("tidyverse")
#install.packages("NbClust")
library(factoextra)    #clustering visualization
library(cluster)       #clustering algorithms
library(dendextend)    #for comparing two dendrograms
library(corrplot)      #correlation between dendrograms
library(tidyverse)     #data manupulation
library(NbClust)       #determine optimal no. of clusters
library("ape")
library("ggdendro")
```

Organizing Mortality Data.
```{r}
data1 <- janitor::clean_names(data_GACod)
data1<-rename(data1, age = ten_year_age_groups_code)
data1<-rename(data1, ucd = underlying_cause_of_death)
data1<-rename(data1, ucd_code = underlying_cause_of_death_code)
data1<-rename(data1, CR = crude_rate)
data1<-rename(data1, CRSE = crude_rate_standard_error)
data1 <- data1[!is.na(data1$population), ]#remove empty rows
data1$cat_code<-substr(data1$ucd_code,1,3)

data1_unreliable<-data1 %>% filter(CR == "Unreliable")
data1_reliable<-data1 %>% filter(CR != "Unreliable")
length(unique(data1_unreliable$cat_code))
length(unique(data1_reliable$cat_code))

data1_by_ucd_code<-data1 %>% 
  group_by(gender,ucd_code) %>%
  summarise(deaths=sum(deaths))

deaths_by_gender_ucd_code<-melt(data1_by_ucd_code,id=c("ucd_code","gender"))
deaths_by_gender_ucd_code<-dcast(deaths_by_gender_ucd_code,ucd_code ~ gender)
deaths_by_gender_ucd_code[is.na(deaths_by_gender_ucd_code)] <- 0
deaths_by_gender_ucd_code$Total<-deaths_by_gender_ucd_code$Female+deaths_by_gender_ucd_code$Male

length(unique(data1$cat_code))
```
Cleaning the lifetime data as well.
```{r}
life1 <- janitor::clean_names(Lifetime)
life1<-rename(life1, ucd = underlying_cause_of_death)
life1<-rename(life1, ucd_code = underlying_cause_of_death_code)
life1<-rename(life1, CR = crude_rate)
life1<-rename(life1, CRSE = crude_rate_standard_error)
life1 <- life1[!is.na(life1$population), ]#remove empty rows
life1$cat_code<-substr(life1$ucd_code,1,3)

life2<-life1 %>% 
  group_by(gender,cat_code) %>% 
  summarise(deaths = sum(deaths),population=population)
life2<-distinct(life2)

length(unique(life1$ucd_code))

```



Organizing code details data

```{r}
codes$cat_code<-substr(codes$ucd_code,1,3)

hierarchy<-distinct(codes[,c(2,4,6,9)])

```

Aggregate number of deaths by cat_code and age group.
```{r}
deaths_by_age_code<-data1 %>% 
  group_by(age, cat_code) %>% 
  summarise(deaths = sum(deaths))
deathcheck<-dcast(deaths_by_age_code,cat_code ~ age)
```

Identify causes of death that do not have sufficient deaths to reliably calculate mortality rates for QCing the data. Typically CDC sets this value at 20 deaths per year to calculate reliable mortality. However we have two groups to consider, males and females. Somewhere within 400-800 deaths should give reliable data. We do not do this by sex however as doing so we would lose codes where males or females have extremely low deaths in comparison to the other group.
```{r}
deathcheck$mincheck<-apply(deathcheck[,2:6], 1, FUN = min)
keep400<-as.data.frame(deathcheck[deathcheck$mincheck>=400,])
keep400 <- keep400[complete.cases(keep400),]
reliable400<-unique(keep400$cat_code)
keep800<-as.data.frame(deathcheck[deathcheck$mincheck>=800,])
keep800 <- keep800[complete.cases(keep800),]
reliable800<-unique(keep800$cat_code)
lessreliable<-setdiff(reliable400,reliable800)
```
Cutoff of 400 (20 deaths per age group per year) yields 297 codes
Cutoff of 800 (20 deaths per age group per sex per year) yields 222 codes
75 codes are less reliable

Remove unreliable codes.
```{r}
overlap1<-(data1$cat_code %in% reliable400)
data1$remove<-overlap1
codes_keep<-data1[data1$remove != "FALSE",]
codes_keep<-codes_keep[,-c(2,3,6)]
length(unique(codes_keep$cat_code))
```

Causes of death with one gender missing are female- or male- specific. Put <zero> deaths in for the gender that cannot die of these causes. 1 will prevent NaN's from resulting later from log correction. C51-C58 are female organ cancers; C60-C63 are male organ cancers.
```{r}
Fspecific<-c("C51","C52","C53","C54","C55","C56","C57","C58")
Mspecific<-c("C60","C61","C62","C63")
overlap1<-(deaths_by_age_code_gender$cat_code %in% Fspecific)
deaths_by_age_code_gender$Fspecific<-overlap1
overlap1<-(deaths_by_age_code_gender$cat_code %in% Mspecific)
deaths_by_age_code_gender$Mspecific<-overlap1
codes_Fspecific<-deaths_by_age_code_gender[deaths_by_age_code_gender$Fspecific == "TRUE",]
codes_Mspecific<-deaths_by_age_code_gender[deaths_by_age_code_gender$Mspecific == "TRUE",]
codes_Fspecific[,c(3:7)]<-1
codes_Fspecific$gender<-"Male"
codes_Mspecific[,c(3:7)]<-1
codes_Mspecific$gender<-"Female"
deaths_by_age_code_gender<-rbind(deaths_by_age_code_gender,codes_Fspecific,codes_Mspecific)
deaths_by_age_code_gender$Fspecific<-NULL
deaths_by_age_code_gender$Mspecific<-NULL
table(deaths_by_age_code_gender$cat_code)
Ncodes<-length(unique(deaths_by_age_code_gender$cat_code))
```
Data is now complete.

Calculate log mortality by sex.
```{r}
melt<-melt(deaths_by_age_code_gender, id=c("cat_code","gender"))
melt<-rename(melt, age = variable)
melt<-rename(melt, deaths = value)
melt<-merge(melt,pop,by=c("gender","age"))
melt$MR<-melt$deaths/melt$population*100000
melt$logMR<-log(melt$MR)
logMR<-melt[,c(1,2,3,7)]
length(unique(logMR$cat_code))
```
Calculate instantaneous mortality by sex ?? 
Per Daniel: "For Gompertz models, we use an approximation of the ‘instantaneous mortality rate’ µ(x). Where q(x) is the mortality rate per year (or large unit time), µ(x) is the mortality as the delta-x --> 0 (like the slope dx in calculus). And it is this that we use for Gompertz models. To get there, we use the approximation µ(x) = -ln(p(x)) (i.e. natural log of p(x)), where p(x) is 1 - q(x).

Skip for now, Not sure how to get past the negative numbers that are generated with p(x) and thus giving NaNs for the -log...

```{r}

left_join(logMR_by_gender, logMR_by_gender_life, by='cat_code')->logMR_by_gender
```

Centering data for clustering.
```{r}
logMRdiff_by_age<-dcast(logMR_by_gender[,c(1,2,5)], cat_code ~ age)
logMRdiff_by_age$cat_code->row.names(logMRdiff_by_age)
logMRdiff_by_age$cat_code<-NULL
logMRdiff_by_cat<-as.data.frame(t(logMRdiff_by_age))
logMRdiff_by_cat_centered<-as.data.frame(scale(logMRdiff_by_cat,center=T,scale=F))
logMRdiff_by_cat_centered_scaled<-as.data.frame(scale(logMRdiff_by_cat,center=T,scale=T))
logMRdiff_by_age_centered<-as.data.frame(t(logMRdiff_by_cat_centered))
logMRdiff_by_age_centered_scaled<-as.data.frame(t(logMRdiff_by_cat_centered_scaled))
CoD<-logMRdiff_by_age_centered
CoD_codes<-CoD
CoD_codes$cat_code<-row.names(CoD_codes)
write.csv(CoD_codes,"Data_centered.csv",row.names = F)

```
Performing Hierarchical Clustering using different methods.
```{r}
hc_d <- diana(CoD) #Diana doesn't work great
hc_a_average <- agnes(CoD,method="average")
hc_a_complete <- agnes(CoD,method="complete")
hc_a_ward <- agnes(CoD,method="ward")
hc_a_weighted <- agnes(CoD,method="weighted")
hc_a_gaverage <- agnes(CoD,method="gaverage")
```

extended pairs code
```{r}
panel.cor <- function(x, y, digits = 2, prefix = "", cex.cor, ...)
{
  usr <- par("usr"); on.exit(par(usr))
  par(usr = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
  r <- abs(cor(x, y,use="pairwise.complete.obs"))
  txt <- format(c(r, 0.123456789), digits = digits)[1]
  txt <- paste0(prefix, txt)
  if(missing(cex.cor)) cex.cor <- 0.8/strwidth(txt)
  text(0.5, 0.5, txt, cex = cex.cor * r)
}
```
